title: The Perfect Ledger
premise: Insurance investigator Sebastian Dravenmoor, whose photographic memory has made him the unofficial keeper of Hollowmere's secrets, is handed a cold case: the disappearance of Clara Voss seven years ago. When her recovered diary contains entries written after the date she vanished, Sebastian realizes someone is still writing in her voice — and that her final entries encode a ledger of the town's most powerful citizens' crimes. As the annual Founders' Anniversary Dinner approaches, Sebastian decodes the ledger, discovers Clara is alive and hiding as its silent accountant, and must choose between exposing her vigilante justice or protecting the town's fragile peace; he chooses a third path, publishing the ledger anonymously while helping Clara vanish for good.
about_author: H. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former forensic auditor who spent a decade untangling financial crimes before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town whose own archives they have never fully trusted.

chapters.title: Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Sebastian Dravenmoor's POV. Reopening the Voss file at the request of the police chief, Sebastian recalls — perfectly — every detail of the day Clara disappeared, including one detail no one ever asked about: a green ledger book in her bag. The emotional beat is the unease of a man whose flawless memory becomes a liability.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The diary returned with Clara's effects contains dated entries continuing three weeks past her disappearance, in handwriting Sebastian matches to Clara's from a single glance. He realizes either she lived on in secret or someone impersonates her with intimate knowledge. Beat: obsession takes root.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Sebastian interviews townsfolk, cross-referencing their alibis against his memory of seven years ago. Each interview reveals a petty crime — bribes, forged deeds, a covered-up death — all connected to Founders' Circle families. Beat: the town's polished surface begins to crack under his gaze.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introduces an unnamed diarist watching Sebastian investigate, writing him into Clara's diary in real time. The diarist knows his routines, his filing system, his guilt over a case he once buried. Beat: hunter becomes hunted; paranoia sharpens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the diary's recurring references to dates and amounts, he finds the ledger disguised as the Founders' Society's public donor plaque — initials and donation figures encoding names, sums, and crimes. Beat: exhilaration curdling as he recognizes his late mentor's initials among the guilty.

chapters.title: What the Chief Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Police Chief Aldous Renner, who admits he closed the Voss case under pressure from Councilman Harrow but claims ignorance of the ledger. Sebastian catches the lie by remembering Renner's own words from years ago. Beat: betrayal; the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Diarist POV. With the dinner days away, the diarist prepares to add a final entry — a confession meant to be found on Sebastian's body if he pushes too far. Meanwhile Sebastian notices the diary's newest entry describes his own kitchen, this morning. Beat: dread at its peak.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Filed Herself Away
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Setting a trap using a falsified ledger page, he draws out the diarist: Clara Voss, alive, who faked her disappearance when Harrow ordered her silenced and chose revenge through meticulous accounting instead. Beat: confrontation between two people who both keep perfect records — and both know it makes them dangerous.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Founders
chapters.summary: Clara and Sebastian's alternating POVs converge at the anniversary dinner, where Clara plans to read the decoded ledger aloud. Sebastian stops her mid-speech — not to protect the guilty, but because he's already mailed copies to every household, every news outlet, and the state attorney. Beat: chaos erupts; power collapses publicly.

chapters.title: Closing the Book
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, weeks later. Arrests ripple through Hollowmere; Renner resigns; Harrow awaits trial. Clara, legally dead, leaves town with Sebastian's silence as her only inheritance. He files the original diary under 'V' — then burns it, choosing living memory over perfect records. Beat: bittersweet resolution; justice achieved outside the law, identity willingly surrendered.
